It spans the cusp forms of weight 2 for Γ₀(11); a modular form of that weight and level agreeing with it up to q² (the Sturm bound) equals it; and its coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations a(m)a(n) = ∑_{d | (m,n), 11 ∤ d} d·a(mn/d²), hence multiplicativity and the prime-power recursions. Method: (1) η² has a multiplier on SL(2,ℤ), exp(2πiψ(γ)/12), with ψ an explicit function of the entries modulo 12, proved from the S and T laws and a finite check; (2) for γ in Γ₀(11) the multipliers of η²(z) and η²(11z) cancel because 11 ≡ −1 (mod 12); (3) vanishing at the cusps follows from f¹² = Δ(z)Δ(11z); (4) a cusp form of weight 2 and level 11 with a₁ = 0 vanishes, because its norm to level one has weight 24 and order at least 3 at ∞; (5) the Hecke operators preserve the one-dimensional space, and the coefficient formula gives the relations; (6) integrality comes from the pentagonal number theorem.
entries.title: The newform of weight 2 and level 11

entries.abstract: Rational membership in the complete forty-four-body cubic coefficient locus is co-recursively enumerable complete even for nonnegative coefficients, with point-padding extensions. For rational automata with at least one alphabet letter, the uniform algorithm produces the complete cubic array and the quadratic section whose realizability is equivalent to the universal cutpoint condition. Corollary 5.1 fixes a rational quadratic family from the probability simplex in R28 to cubic coefficient arrays for 91 bodies. Even when a rational coefficient input is promised to lie in the real image of this fixed family, deciding its mixed-volume realizability is undecidable. This is a promise problem on that family, not unrestricted membership in its image. The explicit three-parameter, twelve-body section in Theorem 6.1 has infinitely many boundary planes and obstructs semialgebraicity.
entries.title: Undecidability of mixed-volume realization

entries.abstract: Support and separator constraints for indecomposable graphical-zonotope summands, planar classification, and exact dimension spectra for 3-trees and partial 3-trees, with lattice attainment and intrinsic incidence forests. Includes tree-join and three-hub book dimension formulas, Hamiltonian 3-tree lattice witnesses, and K5-free graphs with full-dimensional indecomposable lattice weak summands but no admissible spanning 3-tree.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for indecomposable graphical-zonotope summands: spectra

entries.abstract: We refine OpenAI's local smoothing argument to obtain sharp endpoint restriction estimates for the unit sphere and for a compact patch of the paraboloid. Let E denote the Fourier extension operator, let n ≥ 2 be the ambient dimension, and put p = 2n/(n−1). For R ≥ 2, we prove the Lᵖ norm of Ef on Ωᵣ is at most Cₙ times (log R)^(1/p) times the Lᵖ norm of f, where Ωᵣ is the ball of radius R for the sphere and the cylinder |x| ≤ R, |t| ≤ R for the paraboloid. For the paraboloid, we work at a fixed frequency in one auxiliary variable and recover a logarithm in the Dirichlet energy estimate. For the sphere, we use both branches of the wave representation to bound the Lᵖ integral directly by the nonnegative term in OpenAI's propagation identity. The estimate is sharp, as can be seen by applying stationary phase to surface measure on the sphere and to a smooth localization of surface measure on the paraboloid. The upper and lower bounds are formalized in Lean.
entries.title: Sharp logarithmic endpoint restriction estimates for the sphere and paraboloid

entries.abstract: Graphical-zonotope constructions, book spectra, prescribed-coordinate criteria and lattice decompositions, together with the sharp least positive real dilation admitting a full-dimensional lattice indecomposable summand for path joins and path cubes.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for indecomposable graphical-zonotope summands: consequences

entries.abstract: For every n at least five, every positive hollow symmetric rank-three matrix lies outside the closure of actual complementary coordinate projection-volume arrays. The entry includes its inertia, strict perturbation and unconditional open-family conclusions. For every 1 <= k < n it also records the exact mixed-volume compactification by finite marked segments and the affine-dimension bound, including replacement of every marked representation.
entries.title: Rank-three obstructions to coordinate projection volumes

entries.abstract: Polymatroidality is equivalent to local equigeneration and an intersection presentation by ordinary coordinate-prime powers, with the exact lower-rank factorization of integral closure. For a nonzero equigenerated monomial ideal whose proper monomial localizations are polymatroidal, the actual integral closure is polymatroidal and its quotient by the ideal has finite length. The maximum hole degree determines actual Koszul regularity, and the least actual maximal-ideal power giving a polymatroidal ideal equals regularity minus generating degree. Deleting one Veronese generator has the complete stated fine and total nonlinear Betti strand. Exact pure and mixed isolators realize the smallest possible degrees and the sharp first nonlinear homological positions at every admissible localization, including necessity of the outer-band generation tests.
entries.title: Prime-power intersections, regularity and sharp local obstructions for polymatroidal ideals

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the equal-weight case of Lemma kahn+ of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900), deduced from the theorem of Ehard, Glock and Joos on pseudorandom hypergraph matchings, and of the form in which it is applied in the proof of Lemma 3.9 (nibble). (1) DesignsII.kahn_plus_equal_weights: for 0 < δ < 1 and k ≥ 2 there is Δ₀ such that, for every real Δ ≥ Δ₀, every finite hypergraph H whose edges have at most k vertices, whose degrees are at most Δ and whose codegrees of distinct vertices are at most Δ^(1−δ), with |H| ≤ exp(Δ^((δ/(50k²))²)), and every family of at most exp(Δ^((δ/(50k²))²)) nonnegative test functions p_j on V(H), there is a matching M ⊆ H such that for every j satisfying the spread condition (every edge sum ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v), multiplied by Δ^(1+δ), is at most the total ∑_{e∈H} ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v)), the covered mass ∑_{v∈⋃M} p_j(v) differs from ∑_{e∈H} ∑_{v∈e} p_j(v)/Δ by at most Δ^(−δ/(50k²)) times the latter. (2) DesignsII.nibble_matching_tests: under the same hypotheses, for every η with 0 ≤ η < 1 and test functions with values in [0,1], the matching can be chosen so that for every j whose support (the vertices with p_j(v) ≠ 0) has degrees at least (1−η)Δ, the mass of p_j on the vertices not covered by M is at most max((η + Δ^(−δ/(50k²)))·∑_v p_j(v), k·Δ^δ/(1−η)). Both statements quantify over all Δ ≥ Δ₀ with Δ₀ depending only on δ and k; Δ₀ is not made explicit. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma kahn+ with equal weights, and the nibble matching for [0,1]-valued tests

entries.abstract: Formal classification of positive-rate independent exponential-clock random greedy maximal-independent-set uniformity for all finite simple graphs on at most five vertices: exactly the five-vertex path is excluded, up to graph isomorphism.
entries.title: Inverse Greedy — five-vertex exponential-clock uniformity classification

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem (Theorem 1.2) of G. Barraquand, "Convergence of the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process to the KPZ equation" (2026). In the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process (QSSEP) on a box of size L in Z (or on Z), a wave function evolves unitarily under hopping amplitudes given by independent complex Brownian motions, and its squared modulus P(t,x) is a random probability distribution on the lattice. The theorem states that, in a window of size n^{1/2} at distance of order n^{3/4} from the origin, the suitably tilted and rescaled measures built from P converge in distribution, in the space C([0,T], M_+(R)) of continuous paths of finite measures with the weak topology, to the solution Z of the multiplicative stochastic heat equation started from a Dirac mass (whose logarithm solves the KPZ equation), for every sequence n_k going to infinity and all system sizes L_k with L_k / n_k^{3/4} going to infinity. The statement quantifies over every realization of the QSSEP and every solution of the stochastic heat equation on arbitrary filtered probability spaces. Since Mathlib has no stochastic integration, the Ito integral (as a limit in probability of Riemann sums), space-time white noise and the Ito-Walsh integral are defined in elementary terms in the statement file. Seven companion theorems show that these definitions are not vacuous and determine the objects: existence and pathwise uniqueness of the wave function, existence of a space-time white noise, well-posedness and Ito's isometry for the Walsh integral, uniqueness and nonnegativity of the solution of the stochastic heat equation. All eight theorems are proved from Mathlib and the standard axioms.
entries.title: Convergence of the one-particle quantum symmetric simple exclusion process to the KPZ equation

entries.abstract: Let g(n) be minimal such that, for any n distinct integers at least two and any set I of consecutive integers whose length is the largest of them, some g(n) elements of I have a product that the product of the n integers divides (Erdős Problem 708). The formalization proves g(4) = 5 and g(5) = 6, stated with exact cardinality as in the source: for four (five) such integers every such interval contains five (six) elements with this property, and for some four (five) integers and some interval no smaller number of elements suffices. Because every such set of n integers has largest element at least n + 1, exact cardinality and "at most" cardinality give the same value when g(n) = n + 1. The formalization proves both forms: the source's exact reading, and the at-most reading with the definitions of the open Formal Conjectures pull request #4388 for Erdős Problem 708, copied verbatim. The general question, whether g(n) is at most 2n or (2 + o(1))n, is not addressed.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 708 for four and five moduli: g(4) = 5 and g(5) = 6

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Andrew Lyasoff, "Another look at the integral of exponential Brownian motion and the pricing of Asian options", Finance Stoch. 20 (2016) 1061–1096. Framing: rigorous reconstruction/verification of the paper’s joint-density, Fokker–Planck, foliation, π/π/2 contour, Yor (1.1)/Rem 5.1, and Asian pricing material. The Comparator family is all 40 proof-chart theorems, each proved using only propext, Quot.sound, and Classical.choice (including time_reversal, Prop 2.2, Dufresne, joint Fokker–Planck, the §4 conditional rearrangements theorem_4_1_pde / theorem_4_1_striking / formula_4_6 / theorem_4_5, the four cond_density_satisfies_* existence results, g_solves_contour_equation, yor_formula, pi_formula, S_closed_form, SfunC.hasDerivAt, hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun, asian_price_formula, asian_delta), together with compared density/integrand definitions. Tables 1–4 are reported numerical data only (definitions, no theorems), outside Comparator. `hasDerivAt_integral_Re_Ffun` uses the tilted-density/Girsanov route rather than global `(u,w)` domination. Project rule: no Lean `axiom` declarations. The §4 rearrangement theorems are conditional implications (they assume the foliation PDE / striking / ODE / Laplace inputs); the cond_density_satisfies_* theorems discharge those inputs by exhibiting a conditional density (Brownian-scaled Yor) that satisfies each of them. Andrew Lyasoff did not participate in or endorse this formalization. Lean was written with AI-agent assistance under Lars Warren Ericson’s direction and review. There is no sorry in the compared Lyasoff2016 development for the Comparator family, and Mathlib plus pinned public Git dependencies supply the analytic/probabilistic stack.
entries.title: Lyasoff 2016 Asian options and exp-BM integral in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Complete positive-response gluing, exact kernel dimension and extremality criterion, unique positive relation, closing-boundary lift invariance, and induced/clique separator capacities.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for indecomposable graphical-zonotope summands: separator

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of regular induced subgraph bounds for finite random graphs with independent, possibly unequal edge probabilities bounded away from zero and one. The selected theorems give two logarithmic lower bounds, and exact-order guarantees for arrays with equal expected degrees, Lipschitz kernels, and bounded-rank symmetric completions. The library also develops the degree-vector estimates, the overlap second moment, and a product model with matching square-root bounds.

authors.name: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz

entries.title: Regular induced subgraphs in bounded independent-edge arrays

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of A. V. Kumchev and J. Y. Liu, Sums of primes and squares of primes in short intervals, arXiv 0801.0130, display 9 on page 2, derived from the assumed hypothesis Eq33Hyp: the mean square bound of display 33 of the paper's Proposition 1, page 8, for the primes and the sifted function of display 34 with the weights f1 and f2 of page 15, the input the paper obtains on page 15 by verifying the hypotheses of Proposition 1 for these functions. For n in H2, the even n not congruent to 1 mod 3, R2 of n counts the representations n = p1 + p2^2 with p1 prime in the window from X - Y to X and p2 prime between half the square root of Y and the square root of Y, where Y is X to the 7/12 + eps/2. The theorem says that for every A > 0 there is B > 0 such that, for every delta > 0 and eps > 0, R2 of n is the main term r2 of n times the singular series truncated at log X to the B, up to a relative error K times log X to the -1 + delta, for all but at most C H / log X to the A of the n in H2 with X < n <= X + H. It is proved on the range X to the 7/18 + eps <= H <= X to the 1 - eps that the proof on page 16 writes after display 55, and on the printed range X to the 7/18 + eps <= H <= X when eps is at most 5/18. The Lean proves itself the steps from display 33 to Theorem 1: the Chebyshev step from display 33 to display 53, the lower bound for the singular series from displays 48 and 49 with Lemma 3.8, the residual estimate of Proposition 2 on pages 16 and 17, and the circle method assembly of displays 53 to 55. Neither Proposition 1 nor the paper's verification of its hypotheses on page 15 is proved here. Binary Goldbach and the conjecture that every large n in H2 that is not a square is a prime plus the square of a prime remain open and are not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md; the proof reuses code ported from PrimeNumberTheoremAnd, written by its contributors, and is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Sums of primes and squares of primes in short intervals: Theorem 1 from Proposition 1

entries.abstract: A monomial ideal is polymatroidal exactly when every monomial localization has an actual linear free resolution. Universal pure reverse lexicographic colon quotients characterize the minimal generator antichain even without prior equigeneration. Ordinary ideal integral closedness together with local equigeneration gives another characterization. The real convex hull equals the full lower-rank polytope, and the actual ideal integral closure is the ideal of all its integer bases. A genuine finite linear presentation together with the prescribed distance-four exchange condition also characterizes polymatroidality. The selected consequences include genuine quotient-socle recognition, field independence, localization of universal quotients, every monomial term order, exact retained-variable Koszul homological-position tests through the degree/dimension and triangular cutoffs of Theorems4.2/4.9, exact codimension bands and attained minimum testing-set sizes, exact necessary and sufficient variable-order coverage, sharp test-number formulas and bounds, fixed-degree logarithmic asymptotics, and sharp uniform rejection fractions with attained examples and independent repeated-test bounds.
entries.title: Characterizations of polymatroidal ideals

entries.abstract: Let ρ and Q be the roots greater than one of x³ − x − 1 and x⁴ − x − 1. We classify the ordered triples (a,b,p) in three inequalities motivated by the inverse fine-structure constant, the weak mixing angle and the strong coupling, with p any natural number. For real roots of monic integer polynomials drawn from the same family, the unique passing triple is (ρ,Q,15) when the degree and coefficient height bounds are (4,3) or (6,2). Both families include reducible polynomials of degree at least two with nonzero constant term. The same triple is the unique solution when a and b are roots of an irreducible monic cubic and quartic, respectively, of height at most ten, with the product ab of norm −1 in ℚ(a,b) over ℚ. Two explicit quartics show where this classification fails. One gives a second pair at height eleven with the same norm. The other gives a second pair at height ten with product norm +1. Both pass at p = 15.
entries.title: Three gauge-coupling windows isolate the roots of x³ − x − 1 and x⁴ − x − 1 in bounded polynomial families

entries.abstract: A smooth full-dimensional lattice polytope of positive dimension n whose edges have lattice length at least n has the integer decomposition property, and over every field its homogeneous toric ideal is generated by equal-sum quadratic binomials. For smooth polytopes with the same normal fan, edge bound n gives prescribed-parity decompositions of interior lattice points of their Minkowski sum. Edge bound n+1 gives the adjoint Minkowski equality. The latter two are the polytope formulations of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3.
entries.title: Quadratic generation for smooth polytopes with long edges

entries.abstract: For E6, E8, the dual E7 lattice, the integral Barnes-Wall lattice BW16, and D_n plus in every even dimension n at least eight, the global minima of every positive-parameter Gaussian lattice sum are precisely all deep holes. The result extends to arbitrary nonzero positive mixtures whenever the literal nonnegative energy is finite at all ambient points. The full squared covering-radius table is proved with actual attainment: 4/3, 1, 7/8, 3, and n/8 in the respective normalizations.
entries.title: Universal cold spots of E8 and related lattices

entries.abstract: For every dimension d at least 3, the least number of vertices of a conditionally Minkowski decomposable convex d-polytope is 4d-4. The formalization proves the universal lower bound, all-dimensional attainment, the literal least-number formulation, and the stronger statement that below this threshold decomposability is determined by the face lattice. Polytopes are actual finite convex hulls with their extreme vertices, and Minkowski summands may have any affine dimension.
entries.title: The sharp vertex bound for conditional decomposability

entries.abstract: A seventeen-vertex four-polytope has a face lattice realizable over a subfield of the reals exactly when that subfield contains the square root of five. In particular, this polytope has no rational realization. In every dimension, deleting a simple vertex from a full-dimensional nonsimplex yields a polytope of the same dimension whose face lattice is determined by the original marked face lattice. Deletion preserves all real realization fields and the density of rational labelled realizations.
entries.title: Realization fields of four-polytopes and simple-vertex deletion

entries.abstract: A lower bound for the number of matchings of a given size in an almost regular uniform hypergraph with small codegrees. For every k >= 2 there is eps_0 > 0 such that for every eps in (0, eps_0) there is d_0 such that, for all d >= d_0, every k-uniform hypergraph H on n <= exp(d^{eps^3}) vertices with (1 - d^{-eps}) d <= delta(H) <= Delta(H) <= d and codegrees at most d^{1-eps} has, for every natural number m <= (1 - d^{-eps^3}) n / k, at least ((1 - d^{-eps^4}) d / e^{k-1})^m matchings with m edges. This is Theorem 3.5 of Glock, Joos, Kim, Kühn and Lichev, Conflict-free hypergraph matchings, in the case of an empty conflict system, stated for every integral size up to the paper's value of m. The proof analyses the random greedy matching process on a finite history tree: the remaining degrees follow the trajectory d(1 - tk/n)^{k-1}, tracked with explicit errors by Freedman's inequality for stopped supermartingales, and the count follows by comparing the probability of each sequence of chosen edges with the number of available edges at each step. The constants eps_0 = 1/(64k^2) and d_0 = max(2, 2^{16/eps}, (19200k^4)^{2/eps}) are explicit.
entries.title: Counting matchings in near-regular hypergraphs: Glock-Joos-Kim-Kühn-Lichev, Theorem 3.5 without conflicts

entries.abstract: For the three-dimensional Newtonian inverse-square field, we determine the exact sharp Cartesian Lipschitz coefficient C3. It is the global maximum on [0,1] of f(t)=(2+6t-2t^2)/(1+2t^2)^(5/2), attained at the unique root t* in [9/50,1/5] of 2t^3-8t^2-4t+1=0. For any finite set of point sources with arbitrary centers a_i, masses 0<=m_i<=M, G>=0 and Cartesian clearance d>0 at both observation points P,Q, the exact Newtonian acceleration g satisfies ||g(P)-g(Q)||_infinity <= (n G M C3/d^3)||P-Q||_infinity. The segment from P to Q need not remain outside the excluded cubes. The coefficient is optimal universally across configurations: for the unit source at the origin it is the least constant controlling all safe pairs. Euclidean radii occur in the physical force law; clearance and force differences use the Cartesian supremum norm.
entries.title: Sharp Cartesian Lipschitz bounds for three-dimensional Newtonian point-source fields

entries.abstract: Two nonconstant meromorphic functions on the complex plane sharing four pairwise distinct Riemann-sphere values, three IM and one CM, share all four values CM, without a growth assumption.
entries.title: Three IM and one CM shared values

entries.abstract: Every graph on n vertices with floor(n^2/4)+1 edges contains, for each 3 <= k <= n, a subgraph on k vertices with floor(k^2/4)+1 edges. For k = 3 this is Mantel's theorem. Dirac (1963) and Erdős (1964) proved it independently. It is the case l = floor(k^2/4)+1 of Erdős Problem 766, on the least number of edges f(n;k,l) that forces a k-vertex subgraph with l edges.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 766: the Dirac–Erdős bound

entries.abstract: a(n) = (1/n) Σ_{k<n} (21k+8) C(2k,k)^3 is an integer divisible by 4 C(2n,n). Zhi-Wei Sun conjectured this in February 2010. Kasper Andersen confirmed it in a reply on the NMBRTHRY list by identifying a(n)/(4 C(2n,n)) with A112029(n−1). Sun records Andersen's identity in his paper Super congruences and Euler numbers (Sci. China Math. 2011).
entries.title: OEIS A173774: Sun's integrality conjecture (Andersen 2010)

entries.abstract: For k >= 4 and all sufficiently large n, g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1, where g_k(n) is the largest m such that some graph on n vertices with chromatic number k has no cycle of length <= m. This is Erdős's upper bound (Mathematika 1962, Theorem 1) in the form his printed proof gives. Erdős's g_k(n) is the largest girth, one more than the g_k(n) used here, so the formal bound is one weaker than Theorem 1 as printed. With Erdős's lower bound of order log n, it shows that g_k(n) has order log n. Whether g_k(n)/log n converges is the open Erdős Problem 626.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 626: Erdős's upper bound g_k(n) <= 2 log n / log(k−2) + 1

entries.abstract: For a prime p, B(n + (p^p − 1)/(p − 1)) ≡ B(n) (mod p) (Touchard 1933, Hall 1934, Williams 1945). The periods conjectured by G. C. Greubel in OEIS A146107, A146109, A146113, A146119 and A146121 (p = 17, 19, 23, 29, 31) are instances; OEIS already marks them correct. Minimality is not claimed.
entries.title: Bell numbers modulo a prime are periodic with period (p^p−1)/(p−1) (Touchard, Hall)

entries.abstract: For arbitrary real positive semidefinite matrices A_i whose sum is at most n I, the uniform average W of ordered products of m distinct matrices satisfies -I <= W <= I when n >= 2 ceil(m/2)^2. When n >= 4m^2 its lower bound improves to -(1-1/(2m)) I. The formalization also proves the stronger lower bound -(1-1/m) I at the quadratic threshold, the original sine-node criterion, and the cubic-size corollary. The statements retain the original arbitrary PSD and sum-at-most-nI hypotheses. Harmonic decomposition, positive root quadratures, matrix Gram factors, normalized coefficient extraction, and the original rounded-node lower-bound proof are constructed in the repository.
entries.title: When the noncommutative AM-GM inequality holds

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes. For a ray [z] of C^(M+1), a pure state measured in the standard basis, its Born probability vector is (|<e_0, z>|^2, ..., |<e_M, z>|^2) / |z|^2, a point of the probability simplex (also the moment map of the torus action on CP^M). Let mu be any probability measure on CP^M invariant under every unitary; there is exactly one, the Fubini-Study measure. The identity is proved as two volume identities and a frequency corollary. First (born_vector_uniform_of_invariant): for a pure state chosen with law mu, the Born probability vector is uniformly distributed on the simplex, so the Fubini-Study measure of the states whose Born vector lies in a region R is M! times the Lebesgue measure of R in free coordinates. Second, for a given state (born_weight_eq_measure_cell, born_weight_eq_measure_apexCell): for a unit vector psi, cone the simplex from the Born vector of psi; the states whose Born vector lies in the cell opposite vertex i have mu-measure |<e_i, psi>|^2, the Born weight of outcome i. This holds for every unit psi, including those with vanishing coordinates, and the cells depend on psi. Third (born_frequencies_tendsto_born_weights): invariant sampling reproduces the Born weights as long-run frequencies; for pure states drawn pairwise independently with law mu, almost surely the fraction of draws in the cell opposite vertex i tends to |<e_i, psi>|^2, by the strong law of large numbers. The theorems show that Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes; they do not derive the Born rule or say why measurement outcomes follow it. The first form is classical: Archimedes' hat-box theorem for M = 1 and in general the Duistermaat-Heckman pushforward for the torus action on CP^M. The proof does not use the Duistermaat-Heckman theorem; it goes through Gaussians, proves the first form, and derives the second and third from it. The second and third are elementary corollaries of the first; no source stating them in this form was located. No priority or novelty is claimed.
entries.title: Born weights are Fubini-Study volumes

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with O(n log n) edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result is due to Casteigts, Peters and Schoeters (ICALP 2019, JCSS 2021); the formal proof follows the dismountability-only proof of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025, §§2–4), which reduces cliques to bi-cliques and concludes with the one-sided dismountability of Angrick et al. (ESA 2024). The compared statements give an explicit bound of 2n⌈log₂ n⌉ + 4n edges and the asymptotic O(n log n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen. Version 3 restores this statement, unchanged since version 1: version 2 registered by mistake another result of the same repository, the 7n bound of Baligács (2026), which now has its own entry. The proof is that of the library release alpha-0.2.0, in which the O(n log n) bound is an instance of a generic induction on cliques shared with the 7n bound.
entries.title: Temporal cliques admit spanners of size O(n log n)

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of a prescribed 2-factor decomposition theorem for sufficiently large even-regular graphs. The minimum-degree threshold is determined by ordinary cycle-decomposition thresholds for an arbitrary nonempty set of permitted cycle lengths; the order threshold is uniform in that set and in the prescribed list of factors.
entries.title: Generalized Oberwolfach problem: prescribed 2-factor decompositions

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of two probabilistic estimates in the random algebraic template of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900), as explicit finite-N inequalities. (1) DesignsII.TParams.lemma_e_E (Lemma 3.6 e|E with Remark 3.7(i), two-sided): in the template space conditioned on the values of the colours at a set U of fixed vertices, a copy φ meeting U in at most r−1 vertices, whose revealed values are F-linearly independent, passes the tests of colour j with probability between (1−δ)ρ₀(k) and ρ₀(k)/(1−δ), where δ = (q²+q|U|)/N < 1 and ρ₀(k) = N^(r−q) z^(−C(q,r)) ((q−r)!/q!)^C(q,r) |𝒜|^(−1) k/N_act. (2) DesignsII.TParams.thinning_probability (the computation of P(φ ∈ Φ') in the proof of Lemma 3.9 nibble): for families C_i (i < m) of copies of pairwise distinct colours, with covering masses μ_i = ∑_{x∈C_i} P(x passes) ≤ 1, thinning parameters q_i ∈ [0,1] with μ_i q_i = t for all i, and independent thinning coins whose event for the covering pattern w has probability ∏_i (1 − w_i q_i), the probability that the realised covering pattern's coin succeeds is (1−t)^m up to 2^m((∑_i μ_i)² + (m+1)·errMax), where errMax is an explicit maximum, over subsets of the families, of second-order terms (pairs of copies within a family and copies of different families sharing an edge). Both statements are finite-N inequalities valid for all permitted parameters; no asymptotic claim is part of the statements. Mathlib does not contain these results.
entries.title: Keevash, The existence of designs II: Lemma e|E (two-sided) and the thinning probability of the nibble

entries.abstract: On the ground space [0,1], the Latinons of Garbe, Hancock, Hladky and Sharifzadeh, described by Markov kernels with a measure-preserving order map, and the Latinons of the Latinon preprint, described by measures on the unit cube with uniform two-dimensional marginals, are the same objects up to null sets. The correspondence preserves the cut distance, the pattern densities and the entropy, including the value minus infinity; the entropy comparison uses the conditional chain rule for relative entropy, also proved here. Consequently Conjecture 12.4 of Garbe et al., stated with their own definitions and with entropy taken as the negative of relative entropy, follows from the counting theorem of the Latinon preprint. Both the finite case and the case of supremum minus infinity are stated.
entries.title: The kernel and measure representations of Latinons agree

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes. The discrete bilinear Hilbert transform along the primes, H_P(f,g)(x) = sum over n != 0 of Lambda(|n|)/n f(x-n) g(x+n), with Lambda the von Mangoldt function, satisfies ||H_P(f,g)||_{l^r} <= C ||f||_{l^p} ||g||_{l^q} for all finitely supported f, g on the integers, whenever p, q > 1, 1/r = 1/p + 1/q, 2/p + 3/q < 3 and 3/p + 2/q < 3 (the Banach range and part of the quasi-Banach range). The proof is assembled from frozen, author-approved intermediate theorems: a restricted-type tri-tile estimate with an epsilon-loss, the smooth truncated bilinear Hilbert transform on the line and on the integers, a vector-valued bilinear form estimate on R x Z/P, the key proposition p:key0, and the U^3 approximation of the von Mangoldt function, which is taken from the author's earlier formalization of A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes (its import closure is included in this repository, see related_formalizations). All results are checked by Lean and depend only on the standard axioms.
entries.title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes

entries.abstract: For U ∈ 1 + zℤ[[z]] put B(n,k) = [z^k] U(z)^n. Paul D. Hanna conjectured in 2010 that exp(Σ_{n≥1} [Σ_k B(n,k)^(e(n,k)) x^k] xⁿ/n) has integer coefficients for six choices of U and e: B = C(n+k−1,k) with e = k²+1 (A183128), k²+k (A183129), n (A181076) and n+k−1 (A181078), and B = C(n,k) with e = n+k (A181082) and n+k+1 (A181084). The package proves all six, and Hanna's notes that the exponents k² and k²+k−1 (in A183128, A183129) and k (in A181070, with B = C(n,k)) do not give integer series. The six conjectures follow from a general criterion on e, in the style of Dold's congruences along the rays (n,k) → (pn,pk), proved here for the diagonal series and any U; its corollaries cover constant exponents and polynomial exponents under a divisibility condition. A converse shows the non-integrality for a class of exponents. Integrality of exp(Σ c(n)xⁿ/n) is governed by Dold's congruences, which arise in topology and dynamics (see the survey of Byszewski, Graff and Ward, Bull. London Math. Soc. 53 (2021)). The congruence B(pn,pk) ≡ B(n,k) used here is a Gauss congruence for the coefficients of the rational function 1/(1 − yU(z)) when U is rational, in the sense studied by Beukers, Houben and Straub (Acta Arith. 184 (2018)).
entries.title: OEIS A183128, A183129 and four siblings: Hanna's binomial-power exponential conjectures, with his non-integrality notes

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of Forey and Yin's Theorem 5.17. For two definable maps to a common mixed VF/RV base, parameter-definable RV lifts of every pair of fibres with equal bounded residue-field evaluations imply equal bounded invariants of the total VF classes. The saturated canonical equicharacteristic-zero model and small generated-ground hypotheses are explicit. The submission selection contains this one theorem; necessary definition helpers may accompany its vocabulary.
entries.title: Bounded Fubini in algebraically closed valued fields

entries.abstract: A large deviation principle for uniform labeled Latin squares in the full ordered Latinon cut distance, at speed n squared with extended relative entropy as a good rate function. The space retains both row and column orders. For every finite family of strict order patterns and every finite-rate target, the development gives bilateral local logarithmic counts with binomial finite normalization and second-order constant -2. Neighborhood radii may depend on the target and are chosen before the order threshold. Empty compatible fibers have eventually empty finite neighborhoods. The proof includes a uniform lower counting theorem for bounded positive tristochastic profiles and a transportation correction with exact support, bounded entries and l1 cost at most 5/2 times the total margin defect. The entropy convention is Ent = -KL.
entries.title: Entropy and large deviations for Latin squares

entries.abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of Liu, Manfredi and Zhou, "Superposition property in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation" (RIMS Kôkyûroku Bessatsu B99 (2026); arXiv:2508.17106). If u is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞u = f in a domain U ⊆ ℝⁿ and v one of -Δ∞v = g in a domain V ⊆ ℝᵐ, with f and g continuous, then w(x, y) = u(x) + v(y) is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞w = f(x) + g(y) in U × V. For a continuous, degenerate elliptic and sub-additive operator L, the sum of viscosity subsolutions of L(∇u, ∇²u) = f and L(∇v, ∇²v) = g is a subsolution of L(∇w, ∇²w) = f + g. On proper geodesic metric spaces, the disjoint sum of functions satisfying comparison with cones (from above, below, or both) satisfies comparison with cones on the product with the sum metric d_X + d_Y. Mathlib lacks the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem on sums, so its ingredients (sup-convolution, Alexandrov's theorem, Jensen's lemma) are formalized along the way; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Superposition in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation

entries.abstract: This is a Lean 4 formalization of L^3 bounds for the triangular Hilbert form, following a streamlined version of an OpenAI manuscript. This also gives a proof of Carleson's theorem on pointwise convergence of Fourier series, which is also part of this formalization. Theorem statements are human-written, while the proof was automatically generated by coding agents.
entries.title: Formalization of bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform and Carleson's theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalisation, built on mathlib, of L. Niebel, "A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy" (arXiv:2608.02586v3), an arXiv preprint. The fast-dynamo question, going back to Vainshtein and Zel'dovich, asks whether the exponential growth rate of the magnetic field in the kinematic induction equation survives the limit of vanishing magnetic diffusivity; for autonomous velocities on the flat three-torus it is the conjecture recorded as Problem 1994-28 in Arnold's Problems (Conjecture 1.1 of the paper), which asks for a smooth velocity. For sufficiently smooth velocities the absence of exponential particle stretching excludes fast dynamo action (Vishik; Friedlander and Vishik), and the entropy bound of Klapper and Young excludes a C^infinity fast dynamo with zero topological entropy; the paper shows that at Lipschitz regularity fast dynamo action is compatible with zero topological entropy and zero ideal exponential growth. The theorem concerns Lipschitz velocities and does not address the smooth conjecture, which, as Remark 1.3 of the paper records, has been resolved (Coti Zelati, Sorella and Villringer, arXiv:2609.04153). The compared theorem is Theorem 1.2 of the paper: there are an autonomous, divergence-free, Lipschitz velocity field u on the flat torus T^3 = R^3/Z^3 and constants eps0, gamma0 > 0 such that for every magnetic diffusivity 0 < eps <= eps0 the kinematic induction equation dB/dt = curl(u x B) + eps Laplacian(B), div B = 0, has an induction semigroup on the divergence-free fields L^2_sigma whose operator norm is at least exp(gamma0 t) for all t >= 0 (u is a fast dynamo), with an eigenmode exp(2 pi i K x3) b(y) of eigenvalue of real part at least gamma0 and a real solution of exact growth exp(t Re lambda); while every time map of the particle flow of u is continuous and has topological entropy zero, and the ideal (eps = 0) induction equation has exactly one solution group, whose operator norm grows subexponentially. The statement in Challenge.lean uses only mathlib notions and fourteen documented definitions. The repository formalises, in its own terms and with every deviation recorded in DEVIATIONS.md, all statements of the paper except Conjecture 1.1 and Remarks 1.3, 7.5 and 8.4, in about 129,000 lines of Lean in 411 library modules; every audited declaration depends only on the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and there is no sorry outside the deliberate one in Challenge.lean.
entries.title: A fast dynamo with zero topological entropy

entries.abstract: An unconditional Lean proof that a representation-infinite finite-dimensional algebra over a perfect field has infinitely many connected Auslander–Reiten components, using actual finite-dimensional left modules and radical-square arrows.
entries.title: Infinite Auslander–Reiten components over perfect fields

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry. This repository is a thin wrapper: it contains only the statement and the bridge to the temporal-graphs library, the substantive formalization, on which it depends through its lakefile at the commit given below (release alpha-0.2.0 of the library, on its branch prepared for Palomar). The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.
entries.title: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Lemma 3.8 (Lemma ext*) of P. Keevash, "The existence of designs II" (arXiv:1802.05900): in the random algebraic template M* built from independent uniform injections f_j : [n] → F_{p^a}-like field K (j < z), random colours T_e and orders π_e of the r-sets, random A_φ and activations, the number of configurations of an extension all of whose atoms γ(ψ) lie below ∂^γ M* is at least an explicit expectation-type lower bound minus 2εN^v, except with an explicit failure probability (a with-high-probability statement in the regime described below). The statement DesignsII.TParams.lemma_3_8 is fully quantitative, an explicit finite-N bound: the lower bound is |C|·(z+1−kd)_m·(a^m − m²·K_c·(n^(q−r))^(m−2))·p^m − 2εN^v (K_c occurs once, also for m = 2) with a = ω|V(Φ)|^(q−r) − (q−r)·s·n^(q−r−1), K_c = q^(r+1) n^(q−r−1) q^r n^(q−r) (1+C(q,r)) and p = (2N^(q−r))^(-1) z^(-C(q,r)) ((q−r)!/q!)^C(q,r) |𝒜|^(-1) k_min/N_act, and the failure probability is at most C(z,kd)·p_deg^kd + 2exp(−ε²N/(2c₁)) + 2exp(−ε²N/(2c₂)) with explicit constants c₁ = c₁(z,q,r,m,Δ) and c₂ = c₂(z,q,r,m,Δ,Smax), where Smax bounds the sizes of the non-colour coordinates (|𝒜|, N_act, ...) (p_deg = |F|^s N^(s−1) (N−s)!/N! bounds the probability that a colour is degenerate at the s fixed vertices). The bound holds for all permitted parameters. Asymptotic remarks (the Lean theorem itself is a finite-N inequality): every term of the failure probability tends to 0 as N → ∞ when s ≥ 1, 1 ≤ kd ≤ z and z, q, r, m, Δ, Smax, |F|, s, kd and ε > 0 are fixed (it does not for kd = 0 or s = 0). No claim is made that the lower bound is positive: for m ≥ 1 it is ≤ 0 for instance if m > z+1−kd, k_min = 0 or a ≤ 0, and for any m if 2εN^v exceeds the main term (for m = 0, the empty configuration, the main term is |C|). When q > r and m ≥ 2 the correction is at most a constant times n^((q−r)m−1), hence o(a^m) if moreover a ≥ c·n^(q−r) for a fixed c > 0; when q = r or m = 1 it need not be of lower order. The hypotheses are those of the paper: Φ is a Σ-adapted [q]-complex, (Φ, γ[G]) is (ω,h)-extendable (Definition 2.9), the copies used are Φ-embeddings of A = Σ^≤ and those with γ(φ) ≤_γ G are activated with threshold ≥ k_min. The proof follows the paper (Lemma e|E for the conditional probabilities given the fixed vertices, a two-stage Lipschitz concentration for the covering count, the template decomposition of Designs I Lemma 3.3), with the corrections recorded under fidelity. Mathlib does not contain this result.
entries.title: Keevash, The existence of designs II, Lemma 3.8 (ext*): extensions in the random algebraic template

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Solovay-Kitaev theorem for single-qubit Clifford+T circuits. A word is a finite sequence of the letters H, T and T^-1 (with T^-1 = T^7), and its value is the product of the letters' 2 x 2 matrices. There are constants K > 0 and e > 0 such that for every epsilon with 0 < epsilon <= e, every U in SU(2) is within epsilon of the value of a word of length at most K log(1/epsilon)^c, in the operator norm, where c = log 5 / log(3/2), about 3.97, is Dawson and Nielsen's exponent. A second theorem places c strictly between 3 and 4. The word approximates U itself, not U up to a phase. K and e are not computed. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 6 October 2026 (commit 01e973e9). The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.
entries.title: The Solovay-Kitaev theorem for Clifford+T words, with the Dawson-Nielsen exponent

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the two main theorems of Fragkos, Krause, Miheisi and Sun, A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes. For finitely supported f on the integers, consider the modulated sums S_λ f(x) = Σ_{n ≠ 0} f(x − n) Λ(|n|) e(λn)/n, with Λ the von Mangoldt function and e(t) = exp(2πit). Theorem 1.3: for every r > 2 the r-variation of S_λ f(x) over λ in [0, 1) is bounded on ℓ^p(ℤ) for c(r) < p < C(r), where r' < c(r) < 2 < C(r), c(r) → 1 and C(r) → ∞ as r → ∞. Theorem 1.4: the supremum of |S_λ f(x)| over λ in [0, 1) is bounded on ℓ^p(ℤ) for every 1 < p < ∞. The results of other papers that the proofs use are proved in the repository, among them the variation norm Carleson theorem on the real line (Oberlin, Seeger, Tao, Thiele, Wright), the Magyar–Stein–Wainger transference principle for variation norms and the U³ approximation of the von Mangoldt function; none is assumed. The U³ approximation is proved here from the classical zero-free region and the absence of Landau–Siegel zeros, a Lean proof vendored from the openai/math library.
entries.title: A Variation Norm Carleson Theorem Along the Primes

entries.abstract: Two geometric preparation theorems for integration in algebraically closed valued fields. Proposition 3.19 partitions an original-base definable VF bijection into finitely many definable pieces on which it is open-to-open. Lemma 4.8 decomposes an original-Gamma-base definable subset of VF squared into two-cell fibres of a definable map to a finite RV power. The cell positioning graph and both paradigms are definable over the original base together with the output RV tuple. Actual saturation, characteristic, parameter-base and named-value hypotheses remain in the formal statements. The larger repository develops Sections 2–7, including ordinary and measured integration; those additional results are outside this Palomar selection.
entries.title: Integration in algebraically closed valued fields

entries.abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of three statements, all about one field. Let L = QQ(rho, Q) be the field generated over the rationals QQ by a root rho of x^3 - x - 1 and a root Q of x^4 - x - 1, a number field of degree 12 (below, QQ denotes the rationals and Q the root). For a number field K and x in K write H(x) = Height.mulHeight1 x for Mathlib's multiplicative height of x relative to K (the [K:QQ]-th power of the absolute Weil height), and T2(x) = sum over the [K:QQ] ring homomorphisms sigma : K -> C of |sigma x|^2. M(x) is the Mahler measure of the minimal polynomial of an algebraic integer x over Z. (1) The nonzero algebraic integers x of L with H(x) <= H(rho Q) are exactly the fourteen elements +-1, +-rho^(+-1), +-Q^(+-1), +-(rho Q)^(+-1). (2) Every algebraic integer x of L with QQ(x) = L has M(rho Q) <= M(x), with equality exactly for x in {rho Q, -rho Q, (rho Q)^-1, -(rho Q)^-1}; since rho Q generates L (proved in the repository, not compared), the least Mahler measure of an integral generator of L (Dubickas's M(O_L)) is M(rho Q), attained at these four elements only. (3) Let x be an algebraic integer of L with QQ(x) = L such that M(x) <= M(y) for every algebraic integer y of L with QQ(y) = L, and such that sigma(x) is a real Perron number (Lind's definition) for some embedding sigma : L -> C; then x = rho Q (one direction only: that rho Q satisfies these hypotheses is proved in the repository, HeightT2.ρQ_perronNumber_generator_selected, and not compared). The Challenge imports Mathlib only and carries the definition block of the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-10-21-000012 (the field L and its elements) and one definition of this entry (IsPerronNumber). Proved in the repository and not compared, none claimed as this entry's: (i) the inequality T2(x) <= H(x)^2 + n - 1 for x in a number field of degree n, which is Lemma 6 of Dubickas (Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 39 (2023)) applied to the squares max(1, |sigma x|)^2; (ii) its case of equality, T2(x) = H(x)^2 + (n - 1) exactly when x is a root of unity (for n >= 2; HeightT2.sum_norm_sq_eq_mulHeight₁_sq_add_iff); Lemma 6 states no case of equality, no statement of it in print was located (README.md, "Relation to the literature", lists where it was searched) and novelty is not claimed; (iii) the identity that, for subfields K1, K2 of a number field E, linearly disjoint over QQ with K1 v K2 = E, the T2 Gram matrix of the product family b_i c_j is the Kronecker product of the T2 Gram matrices G_b and G_c of b and c (the T2 Gram matrix of a family b in a number field K has entries sum over sigma : K -> C of sigma(b_i) conj(sigma(b_k))) (HeightT2.t2Gram_compositum); special cases are in print (Popov and Zarhin 2021, Lemma 8(iii), coprime cyclotomic fields; Lyubashevsky, Peikert and Regev 2013, eq. (2.6); Bayer-Fluckiger, Oggier and Viterbo 2004, Prop. 6, totally real Galois fields with coprime discriminants), it is the Hermitian counterpart of the trace-form identity of the author's entry PALOMAR-2026-09-02-000014 (statement 3), on a totally real field the T2 Gram matrix is the trace Gram matrix, and novelty is not claimed; (iv) the coordinate bound (HeightT2.coord_sq_le_sum_norm_sq): with b, c finite and E_ii the diagonal matrix unit at (i, i), if s, t >= 0 and Re G_b - s E_ii and Re G_c - t E_jj are positive semidefinite, then every rational coefficient vector a satisfies s t a_ij^2 <= T2(sum a_kl b_k c_l), with T2 taken in E; for families that are bases it is the bound (2.9) of Fincke and Pohst (1985) applied to the Kronecker product of the two Gram matrices, it also covers singular Gram matrices, and novelty is not claimed; (v) that rho Q satisfies the hypotheses of statement (3). The proofs of the three compared statements use the instance of (i) for L in the copied library (RulerSelection.Emb.T2_le_embHeight_sq_add) and a direct proof of the content of (iii) for L and its power bases (RulerSelection.Emb.T2_coords, from RulerSelection.Emb.sum_norm_sq_tensor); they use neither (ii) nor the theorems (iii) and (iv) as stated; (iv) is proved from the matrix lemma RulerSelection.Kron.kron_ge_diag that they use (README.md, "The proofs").
entries.title: The integral generators of least Mahler measure of the field of x^3 - x - 1 and x^4 - x - 1

entries.abstract: Peter Bala (OEIS, February 2021) defined the polynomials R(n, q) = Σ_{k<n} x^(k²) Π_{j=k+1}^{n−1} (x^(2j) − 1), x = 1 + q, as the rows of a q-series (OEIS A340882); their values a(n) = R(n, 1) are A340883 (1, 5, 91, 6245, …). He noted that, q-adically, R(2n + 1, q − 1) and −R(2n, q − 1) tend to Euler's product Π(1 − q^n). He conjectured that for all integers q and N the sequence R(n, q) mod N is purely periodic or periodic after one term (A340882), and that A340883 modulo m has pre-period 0 or 1 and least period dividing φ(m) (A340883, conjecture 1). The package refutes both conjectures and gives the exact answer. For every q and N ≥ 1 it determines the pre-period of R(n, q) mod N: the maximum, over the primes p dividing both N and 1 + q, of an explicit function of v_p(N) and v_p(1 + q). So A340882 holds for (q, N) exactly when 1 + q = 0 or v_p(N) ≤ 5 v_p(1 + q) for every such prime, and it holds for every N exactly when q ∈ {−2, −1, 0}. For A340883 the pre-period is at most 1 exactly when 64 ∤ m (modulo 64 the sequence is 1, 5, 27, 37, 27, 37, …), while the period part, a(n + φ(m)) ≡ a(n) (mod m) after the pre-period, holds for every m. The proof starts from the recurrence R(n + 1) = (x^(2n) − 1) R(n) + x^(n²). For a prime p ∤ x and x^o ≡ 1 (mod p^e), the first o terms of the sum for R(n + o) vanish modulo p^e and the others match those of R(n). For p ∣ x, the exact valuations v_p(R(n + 2) − R(n)) = c(n) v_p(x), with c(1) = 1, c(2) = 5 and c(n) = 2n for n ≥ 3, give the pre-period modulo p^e, and the Chinese remainder theorem gives it modulo N. For completeness the package also proves Bala's conjecture 2) for A340883: for coprime m₁ and m₂ the period modulo m₁m₂ is the lcm of the two periods. This is the Chinese remainder theorem for sequences that are eventually periodic modulo every m, and it is not claimed as new. The audience is number theorists who study congruences and periodicity modulo m of sequences defined by q-series. Bala's periodicity conjecture for A158690, whose e.g.f. 1 + Σ_{m≥1} Π_{j=1}^{m} (1 − e^(−(2j−1)t)) uses the same products Π(1 − x^(2j−1)), was proved in a recent note (Kallat, arXiv:2609.07238): the sequence is eventually periodic modulo every k with period dividing φ(k). That note gives a pre-period bound that it does not claim to be sharp; for A340882 this package determines the pre-period exactly. Bala's companion conjectures for A340881 were proved in 2026 (umaia1234/agentic-conjectures), and those for A340880 are not part of this package. No earlier treatment of A340882 or of A340883's conjecture 1) was found.
entries.title: OEIS A340882 and A340883: Bala's pre-period conjectures, refuted, with the exact pre-period

entries.abstract: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] sin 2x / (2 cos 3x) (OEIS A002439, Glaisher's T numbers: 1, 23, 1681, 257543, …; Glaisher, 1899). Up to a sign and a factor 1/2, a(n) is the value at −2n − 1 of the Dirichlet L-function of the real character χ₁₂ modulo 12, so these are congruences for values of Dirichlet L-functions. In 2021 Peter Bala conjectured six families of congruences for a(n) and stated the formula a(n) ≡ 23^n (mod 1152). The package proves his power congruences 3)–5): a(mn) ≡ a(m)^n modulo 2^(2v₂(m)+7) and modulo 3^(2v₃(m)+2); a(2mn) ≡ a(n)^(2m) and a((2m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(2m+1) modulo 2^(v₂(m)+7); a(3mn) ≡ a(n)^(3m) and a((3m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(3m+1) modulo 3^(v₃(m)+2), and even modulo 3^(v₃(m)+3); and a((3m+2)n) ≡ a(n)^(3m+2) modulo 9. It proves the formula a(n) ≡ 23^n (mod 1152). It refutes conjecture 6) and determines exactly when it holds: for a prime p ≥ 5, h = (p − 1)/2 and m, n ≥ 1, a(hnm) ≡ a(hn)^m (mod p^(v_p(m−1)+1)) holds if and only if v_p(m − 1) ≤ (p − 1)n. For example, at p = 5, n = 1 and m = 3126 = 1 + 5^5, a(6252) ≡ (1 + 5^5)·a(2) (mod 5^6), so a(6252) − a(2)^3126 has 5-adic valuation exactly 5 instead of 6; this is proved by hand, without computing a(6252). Behind this is the congruence a(n + h·p^(e−1)) ≡ (−1)^h (1 − χ₁₂(p)·p^(2n+1)) a(n) (mod p^e) for every prime p ≥ 5, e ≥ 1 and every n, which the package proves from an elementary alternating-sum formula. It is the classical Kummer congruence for these L-values, from the theory of p-adic measures attached to Dirichlet characters that Blanco Gómez's Remark 5 names, and 1 − χ₁₂(p)p^(2n+1) is its Euler factor. When 2n + 1 ≥ e it reduces to the antiperiod a(n + h·p^(e−1)) ≡ (−1)^h a(n) (mod p^e), a case of Blanco Gómez's Theorem 1 on the values b^r E_r(a/b) of the Euler polynomials (Zenodo 23407292), and the "if" direction for 6) is a short corollary of it. At p = 3 the package proves a(n + 3^(e−1)) ≡ −a(n) (mod 3^e) for every n. No earlier treatment of the power congruences 3)–5), of the formula modulo 1152, or of the failure of 6) and its exact range was found. The power congruences carry the main new argument; the exact range of 6) is a short consequence of the classical congruence above. Bala's congruence conjectures for exponential generating functions are recent targets in the study of congruences for Euler-type numbers and for values of Dirichlet L-functions: Kallat proved Bala's conjectures for A158690 (arXiv:2609.07238). Conjectures 1) and 2) for A002439 follow from Kallat's Theorem 2.6 and Bala's hypergeometric e.g.f., which comes from Zagier's strange identity; they are not part of this package.
entries.title: OEIS A002439: Bala's conjectures for sin 2x / (2 cos 3x)

entries.abstract: Let S_m(n) = Σ_{k=0}^n (−1)^(n+k) k^m C(n,k) C(n+k,k)²; S_3 is OEIS A357559 and S_0 is the Apéry sequence A005258. The package proves Peter Bala's 2022 Conjecture 1, n²(2n+1)² ∣ S_2(2n), and the conjecture in the entry's formula section, n²(2n+1)³ ∣ 3·S_3(2n), for every n ≥ 0. Both follow from stronger statements for every n: n²(n+1)² ∣ 2S_2(n), with n²(n+1)² ∣ S_2(n) for odd n, and n²(n+1)³ ∣ 6S_3(n). These give an extra factor 2 in both conjectures. The constants 2 and 6 cannot be lowered: 36 ∤ S_2(2) = 126, 8 ∤ 3S_3(1) = 12 and 576 ∤ 2S_3(3) = 16896. Bala's Conjectures 2 and 3, for m ≥ 4, are not treated. Divisibility theorems for binomial sums of this kind, including weighted sums of Apéry numbers, are a research topic: see Guo and Zeng (Int. J. Number Theory 2011 and 2012) and Guo's proof of a divisibility conjecture of Z.-W. Sun (Electron. J. Combin. 2013).
entries.title: OEIS A357559: Bala's divisibility conjectures for k^m-weighted Apéry sums (m = 2, 3)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of an explicit lower bound for uniformly row-subsampled discrete Fourier transforms acting on canonical binary-heap tree-sparse vectors. With constant distortion, at least half of frequency sequences violate tree-RIP when 20000 m <= k min(k, log_2(N/k)), with an explicit quadratic corollary. The proof uses broom supports, Fejer-kernel concentration, simultaneous Diophantine approximation, and finite counting. A full-DFT isometry theorem checks the normalization and nonvacuity of the definitions.
entries.title: A Quadratic Lower Bound for Fourier RIP with Tree-Structured Sparsity

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the elementary core of the method of J. Pintz, A new explicit formula in the additive theory of primes with applications II. The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem, arXiv 1804.09084v2, 2018, whose Theorem 1 is E of X below X to the power 0.72. Pintz turns zero density theorems for Dirichlet L-functions into explicit bounds through two new steps, which this entry proves. Theorem K, display 4.41, solves the extremal problem of displays 4.37 to 4.39: among decreasing configurations d_1 at least d_2 and so on, with caps d_j at most e_j and a density budget, a maximiser of the sum of e to the B d_j minus e to the C d_j saturates every coordinate before its last active one. The proof is the exchange argument of displays 8.10 to 8.16, done here with the cost in the integral form of display 8.11, and a second theorem adds for an abstract concave cost that the budget is used up exactly and the last active coordinate solves the residual equation 4.42. Theorem J, display 4.36, bounds the weighted excess of zeros by 1 minus xi over 2 Delta; it is proved here from the analytic estimate 7.20, which is a hypothesis. Two Section 9 statements are proved in the repository but are outside this submission's selected Comparator check: the basic inequality 9.4 in the form used in 9.22, and Case 8, where e to the minus 7 lambda plus 2.87 times 10.4 times lambda to the 11/7 is below 1 for 0 below lambda at most 0.04. The zero density theorems, the estimate 7.20, the existence of a maximiser and Theorem 1 are not proved and not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, Codex by OpenAI and Gemini by Google, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: The exceptional set in Goldbach's problem: the weighted density and optimisation steps

entries.abstract: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] arcsin(tan x) (OEIS A012780). The package proves that every a(n) is an integer and Peter Bala's 2026 conjecture that a(n) mod k is eventually periodic with period dividing φ(k), for every k ≥ 1. It also proves the prime-power congruences behind it: a(n + 2^(e−1)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for all n, and a(n + φ(p^e)) ≡ a(n) (mod p^e) for odd primes p and 2n ≥ e, and the conjecture with that explicit pre-period. It also proves that a(n + 2) ≢ a(n) (mod 8) for every n, so the Carmichael function λ(k) cannot replace φ(k). Bala's φ(k)-periodicity conjectures for exponential generating functions are recent research targets: Kallat proved Bala's conjectures for A158690 (arXiv:2609.07238), and Blanco Gómez proved the φ(k)-period for the Euler numbers A000364, where Bala's stronger claim of pure periodicity fails (Zenodo 23150466, Theorem 2.2). Kallat's general theorem gives λ(k)-periods, so by the mod-8 result it does not cover A012780.
entries.title: OEIS A012780: Bala's periodicity conjecture for arcsin(tan x)

entries.abstract: Let a_m(n) = [x^(mn)] 1/P_n((1−x)/(1+x)), where P_n is the Legendre polynomial; OEIS A339946 is the case m = 1. The package proves Peter Bala's 2022 conjecture that a_m(p) ≡ a_m(1) = 2 (mod p^5) for every m ≥ 1 and every prime p ≥ 7, and with it his 2020 conjecture a(p) ≡ a(1) (mod p^5) for A339946. It shows that the range p ≥ 7 is optimal: a_m(5) ≡ 2 + 625m² (mod 5^5), so the congruence at p = 5 holds exactly when 5 divides m. It also proves Bala's Conjecture 2 for OEIS A361717: Σ_{k=0}^{p−2} C(p−2, k)² C(p−1+k, k) ≡ 1 − 2p − p² (mod p³) for every prime p ≠ 3. Bala's entry lists A103882 and the Apéry numbers A005258 and A005259 as coefficients of similar Legendre-polynomial expressions that satisfy supercongruences u(np^k) ≡ u(np^(k−1)) (mod p^(3k)), and it presents a(p) ≡ a(1) (mod p^5) as a stronger congruence. A361717 is of the same type: A005258(n) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−1) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) and A361717(n+1) = [x^n] (1−x)^(−2) P_n((1+x)/(1−x)) (Bala, December 2020 and August 2026). Supercongruences of Apéry-like sequences are a research topic; see Straub (Algebra & Number Theory, 2014) and the references there.
entries.title: OEIS A339946 and A361717: Bala's prime-level supercongruences

entries.abstract: For a four-point support in Z/nZ with n positive and its full labelled ordered square supplied, at most two fixed labelled coefficients of the ordered cube separate the complete four-point square fibre. Coefficient responses are exact integer values embedded in the reals; they are not binary answers. No query lower bound or runtime claim is asserted.
entries.title: Two fixed cubic coefficients distinguish a cyclic four-point square fibre

entries.abstract: Let a(n) = (2n+1)! [x^(2n+1)] sin x / cos 2x (OEIS A000464: 1, 11, 361, 24611, …; Glaisher, 1914). Peter Bala made four conjectures on it in 2021. The package refutes the first as stated: modulo every multiple of 81, (a(n))_{n≥1} is not purely periodic with any period, because a(55) ≡ 65 ≢ 11 = a(1) (mod 81). It proves the corrected form, a(n + φ(k)) ≡ a(n) (mod k) whenever 2n + 1 is at least the exponent of every odd prime in k, so the conjecture holds eventually for every k and from n = 1 when no odd prime exponent of k exceeds 3. It proves the other three conjectures: the Gauss congruences a(np^k + i) ≡ a(np^(k−1) + i) (mod p^k) for every shift i, with the integrality of exp(Σ a(n+i) x^n/n); a(mn) ≡ a(m)^n (mod 2^(2v₂(m)+4)); and a(2mn) ≡ a(n)^(2m), a((2m+1)n) ≡ a(n)^(2m+1) (mod 2^(v₂(m)+4)). Behind them are a(n + 2^(e−1)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for every n, and a(n + (p−1)p^(e−1)/2) ≡ (−1)^((p−1)/2) a(n) (mod p^e) for odd primes p and 2n + 1 ≥ e. The period can be sharpened from φ(k) to the Carmichael function λ(k): a(n + 2^(e−2)) ≡ a(n) (mod 2^e) for e ≥ 3, so a(n + λ(k)) ≡ a(n) (mod k) under the same condition on n, and λ(8) = 2 cannot be lowered, since a(1) ≢ a(0) (mod 8). Bala's congruence conjectures for exponential generating functions are recent targets in the study of congruences for Euler-type numbers: Kallat proved Bala's conjectures for A158690 (arXiv:2609.07238), and Blanco Gómez refuted the same pure-periodicity wording for the Euler numbers A000364 and proved its eventual form (Zenodo 23150466, Theorem 2.2). The odd-prime congruence is known (Blanco Gómez, Zenodo 23407292, Theorem 1), and the 2-adic period follows quickly from Nishibuchi's criterion (arXiv:2610.11648, Prop. 3.4). No earlier treatment of the failure modulo 81 or of the power congruences 3) and 4) was found.
entries.title: OEIS A000464: Bala's conjectures for sin x / cos 2x

entries.abstract: Four Lean results for bicolored Steiner triple systems. For each fixed number k >= 3 of color classes, sufficiently large compatible labelled profiles with positive class and type margins admit exact prescribed block-type counts while completing any sufficiently sparse allowed packing. Uniformly over such prescribed matrices, the logarithm of the number of realizations has optimal leading coefficient 1/6 in n squared times log n. For any fixed K, the same exact type matrix has K realizations with distinct Pasch counts. For every fixed k >= 4, all sufficiently large admissible orders admit a k-bicoloring. The final threshold is ineffective.
entries.title: Prescribed block types and abundance in bicolored Steiner triple systems

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the finite classification of obligatory triple systems. For every finite edge-indexed simple 3-uniform hypergraph F, the compared theorem proves that F is obligatory if and only if its isolated-point reduction is linear, every hyperedge-node of its Levi graph is incident with a bridge, and every Berge cycle has even length.
entries.title: Erdős Problem 593: classification of obligatory triple systems

entries.abstract: For a, b ≥ 1 and m = a + b let f(x) = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 − x^a)^a (1 − x^b)^b) and u_{r,s}(N) = [x^(rN)] f(x)^(sN). The package proves the supercongruences u_{r,s}(np^k) ≡ u_{r,s}(np^(k−1)) (mod p^(3k)) for every prime p ≥ 5 with p ∤ abm, all r ≥ 1, s ∈ ℤ and n, k ≥ 1, and the same for Bala's variant f⁻(x) = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 + x^a)^a (1 + x^b)^b). As corollaries it proves Peter Bala's 2024 conjectures for A372212 ((a, b) = (2, 5), p ≥ 11), A372213 ((3, 4), p ≥ 11, and also p = 5), A372211 ((2, 3), p ≥ 7, both forms), his 2022 conjectures for A351859 (G₃ = (1 + x + x² + x³)⁴/(1 + x + x²)³, p ≥ 5, both forms), and his general clauses for all (a, b) and sufficiently large p, for f and for f⁻ (both read with the power n, as [x^n] f(x)^n and [x^n] f⁻(x)^n). A372211 at p = 5 is not claimed; it is open. For a = b = 1, u_{1,1}(n) = C(2n, n), and the towers are the classical Jacobsthal–Kazandzidis congruences (see Meštrović's survey, cited in A351859). Supercongruences of this strength for diagonals of rational functions are studied for Apéry-like numbers (Straub, Algebra Number Theory 8 (2014)) and for framings of rational functions (Müller, arXiv:2104.10754).
entries.title: OEIS A372211–A372213 and A351859: Bala's p^(3k) towers for [x^(rN)] f^(sN), f = (1 − x^m)^m/((1 − x^a)^a (1 − x^b)^b)

entries.abstract: For an integer q let a_q(0) = 1 and a_q(n) = Σ_{k=1}^n (−1)^(k+1) C(n,k) q^(k(n−k)) a_q(n−k). Then a_2 is OEIS A003024 (labeled acyclic digraphs) and a_3 is OEIS A188457 (acyclic 2-multidigraphs). The package proves the Gauss congruences a_q(np^r) ≡ a_q(np^(r−1)) (mod p^r) for every integer q, every prime p and all n, r ≥ 1. Hence exp(Σ_{n≥1} a_q(n) xⁿ/n) has integer coefficients for every q. The cases q = 2 and q = 3 are Peter Bala's 2016 conjectures in A003024 and A188457; the first also shows that every term of A188490 is an integer.
entries.title: OEIS A003024 and A188457: Bala's exp-integrality conjectures, with Gauss congruences for every q

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of Wigner's theorem for the complex projective space of C^N. Let f be any map from rays to rays that preserves the transition probability |<psi, phi>|^2 / (|psi|^2 |phi|^2). Then f is induced by a unitary or by an antiunitary (a unitary after coordinatewise complex conjugation), and in each case the inducing operator is unique up to a global phase. Nothing else is assumed about f: not linearity, not continuity, not bijectivity. The theorem is stated twice, with linear isometries (wigner, wigner_unique, wigner_unique_antiunitary) and with unitary matrices acting on rays (wigner_unitaryGroup, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique_antiunitary). Mathlib, at the pinned commit, has no Wigner theorem. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 2 July 2026 (commit c26c0954). Two other Lean proofs are listed under related_formalizations: one for maps on unit vectors of C^n, completed on 13 July 2026, and one whose existence theorem covers complex Hilbert spaces of any dimension, at a snapshot dated 31 October 2026. This proof is independent of both. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.
entries.title: Wigner's theorem for the rays of C^N: unitary or antiunitary, unique up to a phase

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Conjecture 19 from E. DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II (Graffiti.pc) collection, matching the exact statement in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture19.conjecture19). For every finite, nontrivial, connected simple graph G, the size b(G) of a largest induced bipartite subgraph is bounded below by the floor of the sum of the average vertex eccentricity and the maximum local neighborhood independence number sup_v l(v). The proof picks a vertex u maximising l(u), sets e = (G.eccent u).toNat and D = G.diam, and constructs an induced bipartite subgraph as a disjoint union of independent subsets B_d inside the distance spheres {v | G.dist u v = d} colored by distance parity. When D ≤ e, one geodesic vertex per sphere 2 ≤ d ≤ e together with {u} and an independent neighborhood subset I ⊆ N(u) of size l(u) gives b(G) ≥ e + l(u). When e < D, the average eccentricity is strictly less than D, and pairing geodesic vertices from u toward a diametral pair x, y on overlapping spheres (separated by distance at least 2 via the triangle inequality) gives b(G) ≥ D − 1 + l(u). The proof uses only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, with no sorry and no native_decide.
entries.title: Written on the Wall II Conjecture 19: lower bound on the largest induced bipartite subgraph size from average eccentricity and neighborhood independence

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 2.1 of P. Keevash, "Counting designs" (arXiv:1504.02909): there are c₀ > 0 and n₀ such that every graph G on n ≥ n₀ vertices with all degrees even and 3 | e(G) that is (c,h)-typical, with density d(G) > n^(-10^-7) and c ≤ c₀·d(G)^(10^6), has a triangle decomposition; h = 2 (the paper's c-typical case, KeevashTri.theorem_2_1_ctyp, new in v2) and h = 16 (KeevashTri.theorem_2_1, v1). (c,h)-typical means |⋂_{x∈S} G(x)| = (1 ± |S|c)·d(G)^|S|·n for every vertex set S with |S| ≤ h; for h = 2 this is degrees (1 ± c)·d(G)·n and pair codegrees (1 ± 2c)·d(G)²·n (the paper asks (1 ± c) for pairs, so the hypothesis here is slightly weaker). The density and typicality thresholds are the paper's (n^(-10^-7) and c₀·d^(10^6)); c₀ and n₀ are not explicit. Quantitative internals of the c-typical proof: c_e = max(c, n^(-1/10)), goodness parameter c' = c_e^(1/4), at most η = 16c'^2·n + 4/(c'^2·d^16) bad one-vertex extensions of a c'-good set of at most 15 vertices. The proof follows the paper's strategy (random algebraic template over F₂^a, Nibble, Cover, Hole, Completion), with every random greedy algorithm of the Completion replaced by a deterministic potential (pessimistic-estimator) argument. Earlier registered entries are imported as lake dependencies: the hypergraph matching nibble of Ehard–Glock–Joos (PALOMAR-2026-10-17-000004) and the Steiner triple system material of PALOMAR-2026-10-22-000017 v2. Mathlib does not contain this result.
entries.title: Keevash, Counting designs, Theorem 2.1: triangle decompositions of typical graphs

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every ε > 0 and all large natural x there is a Goldbach number, an even sum of two primes, in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(26/1075+ε). The theorem is conditional on two cited results taken as explicit hypotheses, never as axioms, and neither is proved here: LiRow052, R. Li, arXiv 2308.04458, Theorem 2, the row θ = 0.52, primes in the intervals from n - n^(0.52+ε) to n with a lower bound of the right order, with some positive constant since the printed constant differs between versions of the paper; and LiPrintedExceptionalCount, R. Li, arXiv 2407.05651 v6, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n to n + n^(1/21.5+ε) for almost all n. The argument adapts Theorem 7.1 of arXiv 2407.05651 v6, page 27, exponent 21/860 from the 0.525 of Baker, Harman and Pintz. The exponent 26/1075 is lower by 1/4300, and the gain is only the replacement of 0.525 by Li's 0.52. Li prints this exponent himself, as Theorem 7 of arXiv 2308.04458, with no ε and no factor 3, so this is a formal check of a known result and not a new exponent. Li's later note, Primes in almost all short intervals II, claims 1/22+ε in place of 1/21.5+ε, so 26/1075 is not claimed as the best exponent. Both cited papers are used here in their arXiv preprint form. Proved with no cited input: the passage from a count of primes in the intervals below n to a count in the windows from x - 2Y to x - Y, and the combinatorial step from the two counts to a Goldbach number. Added in the second version: the same argument at the exponent 13/600, a Goldbach number in the interval from x to x + 3 x^(13/600+ε) for every ε > 0 and all large natural x, goldbach_short_600. It is conditional on LiRow052 and on one more cited result, also an explicit hypothesis and never an axiom: LiIIIExceptionalCount, R. Li, Primes in almost all short intervals III, Theorem 1.1, primes in the intervals from n - n^(1/24+ε) to n for almost all n. Li prints the exponent 13/600 himself, as Theorem 8.1 of that paper, with no ε and no factor 3, so the Lean checks a printed result, conditional on the named inputs, and it is not a new result. That paper is an undated preprint on the author's web page, not on arXiv, and has not been peer reviewed as far as the packaging agent found. The one new step, proved with no cited input, turns a count of exceptions for the backward intervals into the forward count the argument uses. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude, Codex, Gemini and DeepSeek, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Goldbach numbers in short intervals of length x^(26/1075+ε)

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the main result of T. Estermann, On Goldbach's problem: proof that almost all even positive integers are sums of two primes, Proc. London Math. Soc. series 2, volume 44, 1938, pages 307-314. Let Q of n be the number of even positive integers less than n that are not sums of two primes. The Introduction on page 307 states that, as n tends to infinity, Q of n is O of n log^-a n for every positive a; this is the compared theorem, LeanLab.Estermann1938.main. The proof is not Estermann's circle method text: it bounds Q of n by E of n plus 1, where E of X counts the even 4 <= m <= X that are not sums of two primes, and uses the bound E of X << X log^-A X for every A, proved by Heath-Brown's 1985 route from the Siegel-Walfisz theorem. That bound is already a compared theorem of the registered entry heathbrown1985 of this repository, LeanLab.PNTPort.PsiChi.goldbach_logPowerSaving, whose Challenge states the same E of X bound; this entry adds Estermann's own count Q of n and his big O form, and the Lean closure is the same as that entry's plus one file. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. AI agents, Claude by Anthropic, wrote the lab's Lean code; the ported zeta function code is by the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd contributors, as listed in PORTING.md. It is offered for human audit.
entries.title: On Goldbach's problem: proof that almost all even positive integers are sums of two primes

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proofs, with no unproved steps, of two results from H. A. Helfgott and D. J. Platt, Numerical verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture up to 8.875 · 10^30, Experimental Mathematics 22, 2013, arXiv:1305.3062. First, Proth's criterion of Section 2, Theorem 2.3 in existential form; the converse printed after it, for every such a, is proved as converse but not compared: a Proth number N = k 2^n + 1 with 0 < k < 2^n is prime if and only if some integer a has Jacobi symbol -1 over N and a raised to the power N - 1 over 2 is -1 mod N. Second, Theorem 4.1, every odd number from 7 to T = 8875694145621773516800000000000 is a sum of three primes, derived from the two computations the paper rests on, which are explicit hypotheses and are not proved here: binary Goldbach for every even number from 4 to 4 · 10^18, the verification of Oliveira e Silva, Herzog and Pardi, and for each of the 492700 ranges of width 2^54 · 10^9 of Section 4 a ladder of odd primes with gaps at most 4 · 10^18 - 2 that starts within 2 · 10^18 above the left end point and ends less than 2 · 10^18 below the right end point, the paper's own computation. The entry does not verify any ladder or any binary Goldbach case, so it does not prove ternary Goldbach up to T; it proves that the paper's computations imply it. Ternary Goldbach is Helfgott's theorem and binary Goldbach is open; neither is claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, Claude by Anthropic, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Proth's criterion and the prime ladder reduction for ternary Goldbach up to 8.875 · 10^30

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib proofs of the first lower bounds above the trivial bound n for Naslund's crossing problem (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 174 (2020), Problem 12). P(n) is the least r + s such that the tensor [x1 = x4][x2 = x3] on [n]^4 is a sum of r tensors of rank one along {12|34} and s tensors of rank one along {13|24}; in matrix form, the least rank B + rank R(C) over all splittings S_n = B + C of the swap matrix, where R is the realignment. Over every field the project proves P(n) ≥ 4n/3 for n ≥ 3, P(n) ≥ 15n/11 for n ≥ 5, P(n) ≥ 67n/49 for n ≥ 7, P(n) ≥ n + 3 for n ≥ 4, P(5) ≥ 8, P(6) ≥ 9, and P(4) = 7 (with a split that attains 7). The results are original.
entries.title: Lower bounds for Naslund's crossing problem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the algebraic and functional-analytic core of a proof, by Günther's method, of the Moore–Schlafly theorem (Math. Z. 173, 1980): a compact Riemannian manifold with an isometric action of a compact Lie group has an isometric embedding into Euclidean space that is equivariant for an orthogonal representation. It proves unconditionally, with no analytic hypotheses, the equivariant Günther perturbation theorem on the flat torus ℝⁿ/2πℤⁿ: for a map u whose first and second derivatives have a dual frame, with Fourier coefficients in a weighted Wiener algebra, every small symmetric h is realized as a metric perturbation, ⟨∂ᵢ(u+v), ∂ⱼ(u+v)⟩ = ⟨∂ᵢu, ∂ⱼu⟩ + hᵢⱼ pointwise, with a linear bound on v, and u+v inherits every translation-and-rotation symmetry of the data and is real if the data are real.
